messages.subject: Simulate besagproper effect - gaussian likelihood
parts:
Hi I am performing a simulation study and sometimes I am not recovering my besagproper precision parameter ( in some executions I can recover it but in others not). 
Maybe could be a confusion between precision of the normal errors and the besag precision effects?

I attach my code, my code is similar to the one performed in inla.doc("besagproper") documentation but with a  covariate X.

graph = system.file("demodata/germany.graph", package="INLA")
g = inla.read.graph(graph)
## we will use replicated samples in our testing
nrep = 6
## make life easy; use dense matrix algebra
d = 1.0
tau = 1.0
Q = matrix(0, g$n, g$n)
diag(Q) = tau * (d + g$nnbs)
for(i in 1:g$n) {
  if (g$nnbs[i] > 0) {
    Q[i, g$nbs[[i]]] = -tau
    Q[g$nbs[[i]], i] = -tau
  }
}
R = chol(Q) ## 'chol' returns the upper triangular

b = c()
for(i in 1:nrep) {
  b = c(b, backsolve(R, rnorm(g$n)))
}
i = rep(1:g$n, nrep)

replicate = rep(1:nrep, each = g$n)

x=rnorm(nrep*g$n,0,1)

eta=1+x+b

y=rnorm(nrep*g$n,mean=eta,sd=1)

formula = y ~ 1 + x + f(i, model="besagproper", graph = graph,replicate=replicate,
                hyper = list(diag = list(param = c(1, 1))))
## use 'exact' observations, so we fix the noise precisin to a high
## value
r = inla(formula,
         data = data.frame(y, x=x, i,replicate),
         family = "gaussian")
summary(r)

Regards
